gdm: subsectionRotational transform, volume, and volume-averaged texorpdfstringbetabeta To avoid singular parallel currents on a rational flux surface with non-zero pressure gradient, an equilibrium must satisfy the Hamada condition [Hamada 1962], which requires the line integral øint dell/|Bvec| (where ell is arc length along a field line) to be identical for all closed field lines on that surface.

On any rational flux surface iota(psi) = m/n, where closed field lines complete m poloidal turns (Deltachi = 2pi m) in n toroidal turns, periodicity of sin^2(chi) yields which is a complete elliptic integral of the first kind that depends only on psi and m (and is independent of the initial field-line angle chi_0, as well as tau_1, epsilon, S, and lambda), confirming that the Hamada condition [Hamada 1962] is satisfied on all rational surfaces.

glt: Grad [Grad 1967, Grad 1985] argued that, outside the classical symmetric configurations, no smooth equilibrium with nested toroidal pressure surfaces should belong to a family depending smoothly on a parameter.
Grad's argument [Grad 1967] rests on the analysis of the real characteristics of the MHS system along field lines.
lan: The difficulty of satisfying this condition in non-symmetric geometry led [Grad 1967] to conjecture that smooth solutions with non-constant pressure do not exist unless there is an additional symmetry such as axisymmetry: “...we find it very unlikely that there exist a general class of toroidal equilibria with smooth p…” He elaborated on the conjecture in [Grad 1985]: “other than the stated symmetric exceptions, there are no families of solutions depending smoothly on a parameter.” Variations of these statements and related questions are subjects of active study [Constantin 2021, Constantin 2023, Enciso 2025, Cardona 2025, Drivas 2025, Peralta-Salas 2026].

Additionally, [Landreman 2026] constructed the first explicit closed-form equilibria with finite rotational transform, consisting of (1) a constant-rotational-transform (iota = 2) family obtained by stretching an axisymmetric Solov'ev equilibrium [Solov'ev 1968] along the horizontal axes, and (2) a sheared-rotational-transform (iota'(psi) neq 0) family constructed in elliptic coordinates.

Section presents a constant-rotational-transform (iota = 2) family obtained by adding an odd-in-z term to the axisymmetric Solov'ev equilibrium [Solov'ev 1968] before stretching it along the horizontal axes.
[Landreman 2026] constructed the equilibrium by horizontally stretching an even-in-z Solov'ev equilibrium [Solov'ev 1968], which preserves stellarator symmetry.

In the constant-rotational-transform family of Section , including an odd-in-z term in the Solov'ev equilibrium [Solov'ev 1968] prior to horizontal coordinate stretching deforms both the magnetic axis and the surrounding flux surfaces.

works.t: Analytic toroidal 3D MHD equilibria and steady Euler flows with invariant surfaces

gdm: Two families of non-axisymmetric solutions were recently discovered by [Landreman 2026] as counterexamples to Grad's conjecture, but both satisfy stellarator symmetry.

Additionally, [Landreman 2026] constructed the first explicit closed-form equilibria with finite rotational transform, consisting of (1) a constant-rotational-transform (iota = 2) family obtained by stretching an axisymmetric Solov'ev equilibrium [Solov'ev 1968] along the horizontal axes, and (2) a sheared-rotational-transform (iota'(psi) neq 0) family constructed in elliptic coordinates.
Both solutions in [Landreman 2026] are stellarator symmetric [Dewar 1998].
As noted in Section 4 of [Landreman 2026], constructing explicit analytical solutions that break stellarator symmetry has therefore remained an open problem.
In this paper, we construct two multi-parameter families of three-dimensional MHD equilibria that break stellarator symmetry and generalize the two solutions of [Landreman 2026].

works.t: Counterexamples to Grad's conjecture

lan: Very recently, [Gómez-Serrano 2026] falsified the conjecture by proving existence of non-axisymmetric solutions, with poloidally closed field lines everywhere and vanishing B on the magnetic axis.
Together with the family in [Gómez-Serrano 2026], these solutions provide counterexamples to the formulation of Grad's conjecture in, for example, Conjecture 2.5 in [Cardona 2025].
gdm: In particular, [Gómez-Serrano 2026] proved the existence of non-axisymmetric equilibria with infinite rotational transform (iota = infty).

In Cartesian coordinates, stellarator symmetry is an invariance under a pi-rotation about the x-axis, i.e., Although the equilibria of [Gómez-Serrano 2026] can break stellarator symmetry, they do not have an explicit closed-form expression, which limits their use for benchmarking MHD codes.

works.t: Counterexamples to Schiffer's Conjecture

glt: We also remark that our examples share some resemblances to the recent and spectacular counterexamples [Cao-Labora 2026, Colbrook 2026] to Schiffer's conjecture.
Our approach is closer in spirit to that of [Cao-Labora 2026], but we also ran an independent computer-assisted approach.

works.t: Improving ideal MHD equilibrium accuracy with physics-informed neural networks

glt: More recently, physics-informed neural networks [Raissi 2019], which minimize the residual of the equations over a mesh-free parametrization of the unknowns, have been applied to the Grad–Shafranov equation [Jang 2024, Zhou 2025] and to fully three-dimensional stellarator equilibria with nested surfaces [Thun 2026], where they reach lower force residuals than the conventional solvers.
